$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{ln}⁡(y) & =2x \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(y)) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x) \\ [(x)(\frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{dy}}{\text{d}x})+(1)(\operatorname{ln}⁡(y))] & =2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}

$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent at the point $(0,\,1)$ for the curve ${x}^{2}+xy-{y}^{2}=-1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a point, we use implicit differentiation to calculate the derivative of the curve, assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $xy$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+xy-{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xy)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =0 \\ 2x+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)-2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ 2x+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y-2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ (2x+y)+(x-2y)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{2x+y}{x-2y}\end{aligned}
$$

The slope of the tangent at the point $(0,\,1)$ is then given by

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\right)}_{(0,\,1)} \\  & ={\left(-\frac{2x+y}{x-2y}\right)}_{(0,\,1)} \\  & =-\frac{2\cdot 0+1}{0-2\cdot 1} \\  & =-\frac{0+1}{0-2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{(-2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The equation of a curve is $xy+{x}^{2}=1.$ The normal line at the point $(1,\,0)$ intersects the $y$-axis at the point $P.$ What are the coordinates of $P?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First of all, we need to find the slope of the normal line at the point $(1,\,0).$   Remember that the slope of the normal line, ${m}^{′},$ is the negative reciprocal of the slope of the tangent line:

$$
{m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we will calculate the derivative using implicit differentiation, assuming that $y=y(x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xy+{x}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(xy)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}) & =0 \\ x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+y+2x & =0 \\ x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-(2x+y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{2x+y}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,\,0)$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\right)}_{(1,\,0)} \\  & ={\left(-\frac{2x+y}{x}\right)}_{(1,\,0)} \\  & =-\frac{2\cdot 1+0}{1} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is $$
\displaystyle {m}^{′}=-\frac{1}{m}=-\frac{1}{-2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$ We can write the equation of the normal at the point $(1,\,0)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-{y}_{1}) & ={m}^{′}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ (y-0) & =\frac{1}{2}(x-1) \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we just need to find where this normal line intersects the $y$-axis. At the point $P$ the $x$-coordinate is $0,$ so we set $x=0$ and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{2}(x-1) \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}(0-1) \\ y & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(0,\,-\frac{1}{2}).$

$$
\begin{aligned}
4 x+\left(8 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(8 y\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(4 x\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{4 x}{8 y}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{8}{-32}=\frac{1}{4}
$$

The tangent line uses $m=\frac{1}{4}$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-4\right)&=\frac{1}{4}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right) \\
y&=\frac{1}{4}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)+\left(-4\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{1}{4}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)+\left(-4\right) \\
x-\left(2\right)&=-\frac{-4}{\frac{1}{4}} \\
x&=18
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(18,0\right)$.
